name: Shoe lifts / elevator shoes
lead: Shoe lifts are inserts that raise the heel, and elevator shoes are footwear with a hidden thick sole or lift, adding about 2 to 3 cm for inserts and up to roughly 7 cm for built-in versions.
They are used to add apparent height instantly, and also prescribed clinically to equalize leg-length differences.

paras: The effect is purely geometric: raising the foot raises the whole body by the thickness of the lift. No research is needed for that claim. Clinical studies of heel lifts concern leg-length differences and pain, with mixed and mostly low-quality results.

Large lifts change gait and shift weight to the forefoot, which can cause ankle instability, calf tightness and foot pain, and a hidden lift may be visible or feel unstable. A Cochrane review addresses lifts for leg-length inequality; evidence of lasting benefit in people with musculoskeletal conditions is limited. The height gain disappears when the shoes come off, so it is temporary by design.

studies.title: Shoe and heel lifts for leg length inequality in adults with musculoskeletal conditions
